title: UV Light vs. Air Purifier: Which Is Better?
h1: UV Light vs. Air Purifier: Which Is Better for Your Home?
description: UV lights and air purifiers solve different problems. Learn which one helps with mold, dust, allergies or smoke, and when it makes sense to use both at home.
quick_answer: It depends on the problem. An air purifier or whole-house filter is better for dust, pollen, pet dander and wildfire smoke, because those particles need to be captured. A UV light is better at keeping mold and bacteria off the AC coil and drain pan. Many homes do best with good filtration first, then a UV light if coil growth or musty smells are an issue.
body:
UV lights and air purifiers are often sold as if they do the same thing. They don't. Each one solves a different problem, and choosing the right one starts with knowing what you're trying to fix.

What does a UV light do?

An HVAC UV light uses UV-C light to stop mold and bacteria from growing. It's mounted inside the air handler, usually aimed at the indoor coil and drain pan. Because those parts are cold and wet when the AC runs, they're a common spot for growth.

A UV light is good at:

  • Keeping the coil and drain pan cleaner
  • Reducing musty smells that come from the coil
  • Helping prevent slime that clogs condensate drains

It does very little for dust, pollen, pet dander or smoke. Those particles pass by the light without being removed.

What does an air purifier do?

Air purifiers remove particles from the air. There are two main types:

  • Whole-house filtration, which upgrades the filter in your HVAC system to a higher-efficiency media filter that treats air from the whole house whenever the fan runs
  • Portable HEPA purifiers, which clean the air in one room, like a bedroom or home office

Good filtration is effective for:

  • Dust and dust mite debris
  • Pollen
  • Pet dander
  • Wildfire smoke particles
  • Many mold spores floating in the air

Standard particle filters don't remove gases or odors. For smoke smells or chemical odors, look for a unit with an activated carbon stage.

Which one is better for my situation?

ProblemBetter choice
Allergies to dust, pollen or petsAir purifier or whole-house filtration
Wildfire smokeAir purifier or whole-house filtration
Musty smell when the AC runsUV light, plus coil cleaning
Recurring condensate drain clogsUV light, plus drain maintenance
Visible growth on the AC coilClean the coil, then add a UV light
General dust around the houseBetter filtration and duct sealing

When does it make sense to use both?

If you have allergies or asthma and you live near the coast, where humid air keeps coils damp, using both can make sense. The filter captures particles and the UV light keeps the coil from becoming a source of mold. The same goes for homes with a history of musty smells that also deal with smoke during fire season.

If you're only picking one, start with filtration. Particles are the most common indoor air complaint in Southern California homes, especially during pollen season, Santa Ana wind events and wildfire smoke.

What should I watch out for?

Avoid devices that intentionally produce ozone. Ozone irritates the lungs. California regulates portable air cleaners for ozone emissions, so check that any portable unit you buy is certified for sale here. For UV lights, ask for an ozone-free lamp.

Also make sure your HVAC system can handle a higher-efficiency filter. A filter that's too restrictive for the system can cut airflow and cause problems. Media filter cabinets designed for whole-house use usually solve this with a deeper filter that has more surface area.

Placement matters for portable purifiers. Put them in the rooms where you spend the most time, usually bedrooms, and size them for the room. A unit that is too small for the space won't keep up. Run it on a higher setting during smoke events and keep windows and doors closed so it isn't fighting outside air.

Whole-house filters only work while the HVAC fan runs. In mild coastal weather, when the system may sit idle for days, setting the fan to run in cycles keeps air moving through the filter.

How do I choose the right setup?

Start with what's bothering you. Is it sneezing and dust, smoke, or a smell when the AC turns on? A technician can look at your system, check the coil and filter setup and recommend the option that fits. faqs: Does a UV light clean the air in my home?
Not much. Air moves past an HVAC UV light too quickly for it to treat most airborne particles. Its main job is keeping the coil and drain pan free of growth.
Is a whole-house air purifier better than a portable one?
A whole-house system treats air throughout the home whenever the fan runs. A portable HEPA unit is great for one room, like a bedroom. Many people with allergies use both.
Which is better for wildfire smoke?
Filtration. A high-efficiency whole-house filter or a portable HEPA purifier captures smoke particles. A carbon stage helps with smoke odor. UV light does little for smoke.
Do air purifiers help with mold?
Filters can capture mold spores floating in the air, but they don't fix the source. Moisture problems need to be found and fixed, and moldy materials removed.
